answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed market stall, recorded by the market office. The stallholder signs the permit in person, pays roughly $180 a month in pitch fees, and must answer the roll call when the signal sounds. Ten puppets need ten stalls, ten permits, and ten bodies at the same market hours, which one operator cannot staff at once. A copied permit fails the office check. A banned stallholder finds no pitch waiting, not even a corner under the willow, and a fresh name cannot outrun the record left exposed like a track in the tundra.
